tables.explanation: Analysis stage: run_2.py (Negation run) ModSumDataset.fetch_example applies: if rand<0.3 then 50% chance reversal else 50% chance negation. This is a MIXED reversal+negation augmentation (each at 15% effective probability), not pure negation as the paper implies under 'Negation' row for addition. The paper states this as 'negation augmentation' but the code actually applies mixed reversal and negation for the addition operation.

The paper implies 'Combined (30%)' has higher augmentation intensity than 'Combined (15%)', but for subtraction, both runs use exactly the same 15% per-type exclusive probability. The augmentation label '30%' conflicts with the actual per-type probability of 15% in the code.
